source_evidence: One type of bond makes no interest payments until the bond matures. These are called zero-coupon bonds, because they make no coupon payments.
question: Misconception: Zero-coupon bonds pay coupon interest periodically, like many other bonds.
answer: Zero-coupon bonds do not make coupon payments. Instead, they make a single payment at maturity that is higher than the initial purchase price; the difference represents interest, or original issue discount.
